This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
AWARD Heard on I.A.No.1850/2020, which is an application under Order XLI Rule 19 of CPC for restoring the case in respect of respondents No.1 and 2.
2.
Appeal was dismissed in respect of respondents No.1 and 2 due to the non-payment of process fee.

For the reasons assigned in the application, I.A.No.1850/2020 is allowed and appeal is restored against the respondents No.1 and 2.
3.
In the instant case liability of Insurance Company is not in dispute.
Respondents No.1 and 2 were remained ex parte before the trial Court.

In view of the above, there is no need to issue notice to respondents No.1 and 2.
4.
With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

5. The appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") for the enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.448/2016 passed by the XVI Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) on 06/11/2017, whereby an amount of Rs.4,83,600/- has been awarded to the appellants towards the compensation.

entities.text: XVI Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 13/08/2013 deceased Akash @ Manish along with him family members were travelling from Gwalior to Ajmer Sharif in a Eicher vehicle bearing registration number MP-07-GA-2928, at that time respondent No.1 driving the vehicle rashly and negligently dashed the vehicle in trailer standing on a road bearing registration number RJ-13- CA-6090.
As a result of the said accident, Akash sustained fatal injuries and he died.

Mahendra vs Ramprasad on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126604055/
3
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and offending vehicle was insured by the respondent No.3.
7. The appellants/claimants have preferred a claim case under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- on account of death of deceased Akash at the age of 24 years.
Murarilal and Dharmendra Ratnakar were his employer and the deceased was working as a Conductor and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

The appellants/claimants are the father,
mother, brother and sister of the deceased Akash and were dependent upon him.

8. Respondent No.2 in his written statement denied all the averments of petition by stating that at the time of accident respondent No.1 was having a valid driving licence and vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.3.

Respondent No.3 opposed the claim and denied the averments made in the claim petition by stating that at the time of accident respondent No.1 was not having any valid licence and vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

Owner, driver and Insurance Company of the vehicle bearing registration number RJ-13-CA-6090 are the necessary parties, but they were not impleaded as party, therefore, this claim petition is not maintainable.

9. Learned below Tribunal after framing the issues, recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and passed an award of Rs.4,83,600/- towards compensation with interest @ 7% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellants.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the below tribunal has committed legal and factual error by not considering the fact that the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month and looking to the number of dependent family members, claim amount is on lower side.
No compensation has been been awarded towards love and affection, pain and suffering, loss of estate as well as in other heads.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the below Tribunal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by submitting that impugned order passed by the below Tribunal is just, proper and adequate and not deserve for any interference.
12.
Since respondents No.1 and 2 remain ex parte before the trial Court, they have been dispensed with.
13. I have heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the entire record with due care.
14. It is established from the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record that the accident took place by the offending vehicle being driven by the respondent No.1.
At the time of accident, the offending vehicle was duly insured with the respondent No.3 Insurance Company.

Although respondent No.3 has examined Mahendra (PW-1) in their defence, who has deposed that Mahendra vs Ramprasad on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126604055/
4 at the time of incident, deceased was travelling in a goods vehicle as a gratuitous passenger,
therefore, due to the breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

entities.text: Mahendra vs Ramprasad on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, he categorically admits in cross-examination that he did not produce any relevant document regarding the travelling ticket / receipt.

As per the insurance policy premium has been paid for Cleaner also, but at the time of incident, deceased was travelling in a goods vehicle and the term and condition of Insurance Policy was violated by the deceased,
therefore, the principal of pay and recover is applicable in the instant case.
15. The moot question to be addressed in the appeal preferred by the appellant is, as to whether the Tribunal was justified in awarding an amount of Rs.4,83,600/- to the appellants/claimants.
The appellant No.1 Mahendra deposed before the below Tribunal that his son was working as a Conductor and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month and in future his salary would have been increased.
They have been deprived from his love and affection, service and future income.
His statement is well supported by the statement of Raghuveer (PW-2).

Although no salary certificate has been produced by the appellants, but as per chart containing guidelines / instructions issued by the M.P. State Legal Services Authority, which is based upon the income chart endorsed by the Labour Department, Govt. of M. P., in the year 2013-14 the wages of an unskilled labour determined as Rs.5,400/- per month.
In view of the above, the monthly salary of the deceased ought to be assessed as Rs.4,800/-, therefore, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.57,600/-.

16. At the time of incident, the deceased was aged about 24 years, therefore, the below Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of 18 and appellants/claimants are the father, mother, brother and sister of the deceased.
In view of the above, below Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/2 of the income of the deceased towards self expenses.

In light of the judgment of Hon'ble apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the below Tribunal has rightly awarded 40% amount towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. In view of the aforesaid analysis, this Court is of the considered opinion that looking to the age of the deceased, income and dependency of the appellants, loss of dependency comes to Rs.4,800 +
40% FP -  self expenses x 12 x 18 = Rs.7,25,760/-, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, therefore, total compensation of Rs.7,55,760/- should be awarded.
18. The below Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.4,83,600/-.
Hence, the appellants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,72,160/-.
The enhanced amount will bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal and will governed by the same conditions as contained in the award of the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal including the direction of pay and recover shall remain intact.
Certified copy as per rules.
